description: Mini-tenders awarded inside dynamic purchasing systems and framework agreements (DNS / rámcové dohody) generally do not generate individual high-visibility notices, yet they are how much CZ public ICT and payment-hardware volume is actually placed.

Because each contracting authority chooses its own certified e-tool, full documentation coverage requires a maintained registry mapping banking-relevant authorities (ICO) to their current profil zadavatele host. No such mapping exists yet for this cell.

This pass established the platform layer but not the empirical query vocabulary: no systematic enumeration was done of the Czech phrasings actually used in banking/payment tender titles (e.g. akceptace platebních karet, pronájem platebních terminálů, platební brána, zúčtování, bankovní služby vedení účtů, pokladní systém, provozování platebního styku).

Municipal and regional buyers are a major demand pool for card acceptance and terminals (the confirmed Přerov card-acceptance tender is an example), but sub-national authorities are spread across many e-tools and were only sampled here, not mapped.

English coverage of this cell is thin by nature: NEN offers an /en mirror and TED carries English translations of above-threshold notices, but below-threshold CZ notices and all tender documentation are Czech-only.
Rate limits, robots policies and terms of use for NEN, VVZ and the commercial e-tool hosts were not examined in this pass, and the Hlídač státu API's key/quota terms are unconfirmed.
No authenticated TED API key or tested expert query exists yet for country=CZE crossed with the finance/payments CPV set.
The finance/payments CPV pick-list is only partially enumerated (66110000, 66113000, 66172000 confirmed by name; 661/666/72 branches not fully expanded).

No enumerated list of CZ contracting authorities most likely to buy banking/payment services (ČNB, ministries, Česká pošta, health insurers, regions, state funds, universities, transport operators) with their IČO identifiers.

Utilities-sector (Directive 2014/25) and defence/security notices naming CZ entities were not separately examined, nor were contract-modification notices, which reveal extensions of incumbent banking contracts without re-tender.
The cross-border dimension of the cell — non-CZ suppliers winning CZ notices, and CZ suppliers winning notices elsewhere — has no retrieval design yet.
ÚOHS (Úřad pro ochranu hospodářské soutěže) decisions on challenged CZ procurements were not covered in this pass, though they are the richest narrative source on contested banking/IT awards.
Two candidate URLs (ted.europa.eu/en/simap/cpv, mmr.gov.cz NPO landing page) were inferred from site structure rather than directly observed, and the TED-CSV dataset path is legacy.

Regional-level oversight bodies were not covered: Ministerstvo financí's financial-control/audit arm over territorial units, krajské úřady audit outputs, and Krajský soud v Brně (first-instance reviewer of ÚOHS procurement decisions, below NSS).

The CZ glossary built here is strong on procurement-procedure terms but thin on payments-domain tender vocabulary (e.g. akceptace platebních karet, platební terminály, bankomaty, kartové centrum, zpracování transakcí, jádrový bankovní systém).

EU-level regulator/audit layers adjacent to this cell were not scouted: EBA payment institutions register, ECB/SSM lists, European Court of Auditors, and TED/EU procurement remedies — all of which cover CZ entities and cross-border bidders.
No assessment was made of publication lag: how long after a decision or audit becomes effective it appears in the ÚOHS collection, the NKÚ Věstník, or JERRS.
Reuse terms were not established for the NGO aggregator (Hlídač státu) or confirmed per-dataset on NKOD.
No mapping yet from financial-sector buyer (ICO) to hosting e-tendering platform beyond ČNB. Without this, platform crawling is untargeted.
Private-sector (commercial bank, fintech, PSP) RFPs are essentially invisible on the public platforms; PROEBIZ/TENDERBOX corporate deployments are the most plausible but unconfirmed route.
No assessment yet of machine-access affordances (RSS, JSON endpoints, robots.txt, rate limits, bot defences) for E-ZAK instances, Tenderarena's JSF interface, Josephine, Gemin and PVU.
CEE cross-border mirrors were covered only via Opentender.eu; tenders.guru and any SK/PL regional aggregators sharing the JOSEPHINE/ProeBiz stack were not verified in this pass.

Slovak-language querying was not performed, although JOSEPHINE/ProeBiz is a CZ-SK cross-border stack and Slovak terminology ('verejné obstarávanie', 'elektronické trhovisko') would surface additional deployments and documentation.

No structured, automatable feed identified for role changes / executive appointments at CZ commercial banks; candidate aggregators (ManagementNews, EduCity 'Personální změny', MediaGuru) were seen only as search hits and not assessed.

Career pages were captured for KB, ČS, ČSOB and ČNB only. Missing: Moneta, Raiffeisenbank, UniCredit CZ/SK, Air Bank/PPF, Fio, mBank, Trinity/Creditas, plus acquirers and processors (Global Payments CZ, Worldline, Nexi, ČSOB acquiring) and integrators.
Startup/tech-specific CZ job boards (StartupJobs.cz, Welcome to the Jungle CZ, Techloop) were not searched; these carry fintech and vendor engineering roles that mainstream boards miss.
Several conference sources were assessed from search snippets rather than fetched agenda pages; per-edition programme URL patterns (beyond cardforum's /data/cardforumYYYYinfo.pdf) are unconfirmed.
Vendor-side signals (Printec competitors' and partners' own press releases, case studies and award submissions announcing CZ bank wins) were not systematically enumerated in this cell.

No dedicated Czech trade outlet found that covers cards/acquiring/payment-processing as a beat (analogous to a Czech 'PaymentsSource'); payments coverage is scattered across E15, Bankovnictví, Lupa and retail media.

Industry-association and vendor communication channels (ČBA – Česká bankovní asociace, SBK, ČNB press releases, vendor Czech-language press rooms) were not covered in this cell but are the main disclosure route for private-bank supplier deals.
English-language coverage of Czech banking/payments tenders was not located as a distinct source; searches surfaced only Czech-language outlets plus generic international pages.
Retrieval depth of outlet archives (how far back article indexes and RSS reach, whether HN's archiv.hn.cz is fully open) was not established.

Regional coverage of municipal/transport-authority ticketing and payment tenders is represented only by Zdopravy.cz and Deník.cz; regional dailies and transport-authority newsrooms are not enumerated.

The Czech national web archive (Webarchiv, operated by the National Library of the Czech Republic) was not searched or assessed in this slice, despite being the most likely holder of deep historic captures of .cz government and supplier sites.

For several key structured routes — VVZ/cdz.vvz.nipez.cz distribution, the NIPEZ Registr veřejných zakázek consumer interface, and the ISVZ OpenData download paths — I identified the systems but did not establish exact endpoint URLs, schema versions or authentication requirements.

The contracting-authority side is mapped only for ČNB. The wider CZ banking/payments buyer set — commercial banks that are not public contracting authorities, Národní rozvojová banka, Česká pošta, state institutions with card/terminal estates — has not been resolved to profile URLs or IČOs.

No source found in this slice directly exposes contract END dates as a queryable field; expiry must be derived from Registr smluv contract metadata (effective date plus stated duration) or from framework-agreement terms in tender documentation.

The Registr smluv publisher explicitly warns that its dataset contains personal data and that the recipient becomes a GDPR controller. No handling policy has been defined for this slice's recommended bulk ingestion.

Certified Czech e-procurement platforms other than NEN — Tender arena, E-ZAK instances beyond ČNB, Gemin, e-zakazky.cz, vhodne-uverejneni.cz — were identified only in passing; their statutory XML profile-export endpoints were not enumerated.

DORA requires financial entities to maintain a register of information on all contractual arrangements with ICT third-party service providers, reported to competent authorities; CSRD/ESRS requires value-chain disclosure. Neither the group-level nor the ČNB-facing manifestation of these obligations was investigated in this run.

Cell coverage is uneven across the five groups: Erste and SG are well mapped, KBC and RBI are covered at policy level only, and UniCredit's current procurement owner is unresolved. Second-tier CEE parents with Czech exposure (e.g. other foreign-owned CZ banks and their group sourcing arms) were not addressed at all.

No aggregator or archival layer was located for group sourcing: no supplier-network discovery surface (e.g. Ariba Discovery), no procurement-tender aggregator covering private bank buyers in CEE, and no systematic use of web archives to recover withdrawn supplier pages.

German (Vienna: Erste, RBI), Dutch (Brussels: KBC) and Italian (Milan: UniCredit) are the working languages of three of the five decision centres, and none was searched. Only cs, en and incidental fr were used.

Hiring and organisational signals (group procurement job ads naming categories, tools and locations; CZ-based sourcing roles at group entities) were identified as a route but never systematically collected, partly because the richest surface (LinkedIn) is login-gated and ToS-restricted.

Several URLs in this slice were obtained from search-result listings rather than fetched directly (KBC our-suppliers, SG Sourcing Hub, RBI code-of-conduct PDFs, Erste Digital, the smlouvy.gov.cz example PDF). Only the Erste Group Procurement page and kb.cz/cs/dodavatele were actually retrieved and read.

Ministry of the Interior (MV ČR) and Digitální a informační agentura (DIA) are the actual administrators of the public-administration payment-gateway DNS and of gov.cz portal services, but sit outside this cell's named actor list.

Central-state buyers are split across at least four e-procurement platforms — E-ZAK (MF, ČNB), NEN/NIPEZ, TENDER ARENA (Česká pošta), and commercial profiles such as vhodne-uverejneni/Gemin — with no single crawl covering all document-level content.

ISVZ open data changed format in February 2024 (legacy XML before, new datasets after), and older agency tenders (e.g. the 2017 customs terminal contract) are reachable mainly as loose PDFs on agency sites.

No CPV code shortlist was established for state purchases of card acceptance, payment gateways, POS terminals and payment-system integration, so open-data filtering is currently keyword-only and will over- and under-match.
Hlídač státu offers full data and an API but points commercial users to a licensing contact; reuse terms for commercial market intelligence were not established in this pass.

Only a subset of the 13 kraje + Praha were located concretely (MSK, Karlovarský, Jihomoravský, Plzeňský central purchasing). Středočeský, Ústecký, Liberecký, Královéhradecký, Pardubický, Vysočina, Jihočeský, Olomoucký, Zlínský regional profiles were not individually pinned down.

Statutární města beyond Prague/Brno (Ostrava, Plzeň, Liberec, Olomouc, Hradec Králové, Pardubice, České Budějovice, Ústí nad Labem, Zlín, Havířov, Karviná, Most, Opava, Jihlava, Teplice, Chomutov, Frýdek-Místek, Děčín, Karlovy Vary, Mladá Boleslav, Přerov, Prostějov) were only reached via aggregator listings, not their own profiles.

School canteen payments, waste-fee and local-fee (místní poplatky) cashless collection, and municipal POS acceptance for counters (podatelna/pokladna) were part of the cell rationale but produced no concrete tender sources in this pass.
Prague městské části: only Praha 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 10, 19 were observed; the full set of 57 (22 administrative) districts is unmapped.

No robots.txt / rate-limit / ToS assessment was performed for the commercial platform families (Tender arena, e-zakazky.cz, vhodne-uverejneni.cz, profilzadavatele.cz) that host most municipal profiles.

No validated Czech keyword/CPV taxonomy yet exists for identifying banking and payment contracts in free-text 'predmet smlouvy' fields (e.g. 'vedeni bezneho uctu', 'platebni terminal', 'akceptace platebnich karet', 'zpracovani hotovosti', 'bankovni sluzby', 'platebni brana', 'POS terminal', 'ekvajring/acquiring').

The banking/payments supplier watchlist (ICOs for Ceska sporitelna, Komercni banka, CSOB, Moneta, Raiffeisenbank, UniCredit CZ, Fio, J&T, plus acquirers/terminal vendors such as Global Payments, Worldline, Monet+, Printec and gateway providers) was not yet resolved to ICO in this pass.

How amendments (dodatky) are linked to parent contracts in the register metadata was not established. Amendments are where real value drift and contract extensions appear, which is central to this cell's rationale.

The join between the contract register (executed contracts) and the tender/award registers (NEN, VVZ, TED) was not investigated in this cell, so we cannot yet trace a notice through to its signed contract and value.

Coverage of state-owned and quasi-public banks/entities (e.g. Ceska exportni banka, Narodni rozvojova banka, Ceska posta) as either buyers or suppliers of payment services in the register was not probed.
Terms of use and rate limits for the two key third-party layers (Hlidac statu API, registrysmluv.cz) were not read, and no API token was obtained.
No archival strategy exists to counter the register's retroactive rewriting of historical dumps and withdrawal of contracts, and no third-party immutable archive of the register was identified.

Regional/municipal transport undertakings (dopravní podniky in Brno, Ostrava, Plzeň, Olomouc, Liberec, Ústí, České Budějovice, etc.) and the integrated-transport organisers (ROPID, IDSK, KORDIS, IDOK) were not individually enumerated, yet each is a sectoral entity tendering EOC/contactless card acceptance.

Large state/teaching hospitals (VFN, FN Motol, FN Brno, IKEM, ÚVN and the direktly-managed 'přímo řízené organizace' of the Ministry of Health) were not individually mapped to buyer profiles in this pass.

Health insurers beyond VZP, ZP MV ČR and OZP (ČPZP 205, VoZP 201, RBP 213, ZPŠ 209) were not resolved to buyer profiles; also Česká pošta (state-owned, SIPO operator and a major cash/payment node) was not covered in this cell's pass.
No CPV code list has been validated against actual Czech notices for payment-acceptance/treasury subject matter.

Below-threshold and exempted purchases (VZMR — veřejné zakázky malého rozsahu) by sectoral entities are largely invisible in the gazette, and payment-acceptance deals are often revenue-share rather than fixed-price, which can keep them under thresholds.

English-language coverage of this cell is structurally thin: only TED and a few commercial aggregators publish in EN, and no EN term reliably maps to 'odbavovací systém' or 'akceptace platebních karet'.

The Erste Group Procurement Czech subsidiary — the entity that actually buys on behalf of Česká spořitelna — has not been identified by legal name, IČO, or registered address. The alias 's ProServ' surfaced via LinkedIn but was not verified against a register.
csob.cz is unreachable with a plain HTTP fetcher (uniform HTTP 500), leaving the largest CZ bank's procurement policy documented only through third-party corroboration.
No named, entry-resolved e-sourcing platform for any of the eight banks. This is the difference between knowing a bank's procurement philosophy and knowing when it is buying.
Air Bank, Partners Banka, Fio banka and UniCredit CZ have no discoverable supplier channel — four of eight named banks with effectively zero coverage.

The Czech-language supplier document set on Erste Group's site is behind a JavaScript country drop-down that a non-rendering fetch cannot expand, so the cs Supplier Code of Conduct and General Terms and Conditions of Purchase applicable to Česká spořitelna were not retrieved.

Only current versions of supplier codes and terms were located; no historical versions or change logs. Without a baseline, the diff-based monitoring recommended for KB, KBC, Erste and RBI cannot detect the first change it sees.

The cell has no route to award-level or spend-level data. No CZ private bank publishes contract awards, supplier lists, or category spend, and none appears on public e-procurement platforms as a buyer.
Pointer-class sources are thin. Only one genuinely productive Czech pointer was found (byznysprospolecnost.cz / byznysudrzitelnost.cz), and it was discovered incidentally rather than systematically.

Several named target vendors were not individually enumerated in this pass: Nexi/Nets, Global Payments (CZ entity newsroom), Gemalto/Thales CZ, Monet+ own site (monetplus.cz), Trask, Ness CZ, Adyen CZ, Teya, SumUp CZ, FiskalPRO, Euronet (large CZ independent ATM deployer), Loomis/Brink's (cash handling).
Euronet Worldwide and other independent ATM deployers (IADs) operate significant CZ estates; they were not covered in this pass and are a distinct source category from bank-vendor wins.

The cell covers 'deployed at a Czech bank OR retailer', but all queries this pass were bank-oriented. Retail POS/self-checkout wins (Albert, Lidl, Kaufland, Tesco/Tesco CZ, Globus, Rohlik) at vendors like Diebold Nixdorf Retail, NCR Voyix, Printec, Toshiba/Elera were not searched.
Vendor case studies and logo pages are routinely deleted when a contract ends, and no archival capture path was established in this pass.

Vendor-customer joint appearances at CZ/CEE industry events (ATMIA CEE, Payments/Banking conferences, Zlatá koruna awards, Bankovnictví awards) were not covered; joint speaking slots often disclose deployments before any press release.

Several URLs recorded here are section/root paths inferred from search results (e.g. Auriga press-release index, Cleverlance /cz/novinky/, Printec group case studies, systemonline.cz section root, penize.cz /tiskove-zpravy) rather than pages fetched in this pass.
Acquirer/PSP layer is only partially mapped: Besteron, Monri/Payten-type regional processors, Nexi/Nets footprint in CZ, and terminal-estate vendors were not covered.

EU-level tender channel (TED) was not searched for CZ payments notices, and neither was the ČNB free-information (Act 106/1999) disclosure archive, which sometimes discloses supplier names withheld elsewhere.
Scheme certification and partner programmes (Mastercard/Visa vendor certification, tokenisation service providers, 3DS ACS vendors approved for CZ issuers) have no located source at all.

Local-language coverage was achieved for registers, associations and PSPs, but no Czech-language terminology was found or used for scheme certification concepts (certifikace akceptačního zařízení, ACS/3DS vendor approval).
No URL in this slice was fetched; all entries rest on search-result metadata and snippets.
ASPPS (payment service providers association) membership and activity level unverified; only registry records and a legacy http homepage were seen.

English-language variants were confirmed only for ICT UNIE (/en/ictu-members), Czech Fintech Association (/en/), APEK (/en) and SPIR (legacy old.spir.cz). ČBA, ČLFA, SBK, AVZ and AKAT member lists were seen only in Czech.
No association covering cash handling / ATM operations / security printing (e.g. cash-in-transit or ATM-operator bodies) was found, and no crypto/digital-asset association was searched in this pass.
Member rosters were confirmed to exist but were not fully extracted in this pass for AVZ, SBK, APEK, AKAT, ČAP and SPIR (only sampled names observed via search snippets).
Chamber-of-commerce and municipal-union coverage is spread over ~57 OHK sites and 13+ regional municipal unions, each with its own page layout.
APEK operates a login-gated členská zóna; the extent of member data behind it is unknown.
